// Part: room: bedroom 5 (east rear bedroom). Interior air x55..60, z54..60, floor y11, air y11..16.
// Entered from the west wall (door x54 z57, lane kept clear at x55 z56..57); keep-clear cells for the other
// candidate doorways (north x56 z53, east x61 z56..57) stay free too. Bed on the west wall (head x55 z58), barrel
// nightstand with a lantern, a two-chest dresser on the north wall, a red rug in the middle, a barrel side table in
// the SE corner with a flower pot, and a hanging lantern from the plate.
import { layers, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
import { porchLantern } from "../vocab.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // one layer per row of y: rows run along +x (x55..60), successive rows along +z (z54..60)
  layers(g, [55, 11, 54], {
    C: ["chest", { facing: "south" }],
    R: "red_carpet",
    K: "barrel",
    P: "flower_pot",
    N: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
  }, [
    [
      "..CC..", // z54: dresser chests on the north wall (x57, x58); x56 kept clear for the north doorway
      "..RRR.", // z55: red rug x57..59, z55..57
      "..RRR.", // z56
      "..RRR.", // z57: west lane (x55) and east doorway cells (x60) stay free
      "......", // z58: bed goes here (placed by bed())
      "K.....", // z59: nightstand barrel at x55 (south of the bed head)
      ".....K", // z60: side table barrel at x60 (SE corner)
    ],
  ]);
  layers(g, [55, 12, 54], {
    N: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
    P: "flower_pot",
  }, [
    [
      "......",
      "......",
      "......",
      "......",
      "......",
      "N.....", // lantern standing on the bedside barrel
      ".....P", // flower pot on the side table
    ],
  ]);
  // the bed: foot at x56, head at x55 (pillow end against the west wall), both at z58
  bed(g, [56, 11, 58], "west", "red");
  // the ceiling lantern: iron_chain at y16 under the plate, hanging lantern at y15, over the rug
  porchLantern(g, 57, 16, 57);
  // a second hanging lantern in the north-east corner, where the first one's light runs thin
  porchLantern(g, 60, 16, 54);
}
----

input.summary:
room-22 (bedroom 5) is not built: all 21 of its writes are refused, so it places 0 blocks. The mansion shell owns all 252 cells of its box (x55..60, y11..16, z54..60) as carved air, and runParts locks those cells.
No off-palette ids in room-22 (every id is in palette.json), though that check never ran because every write was refused first. make.sh still writes build.nbt, but without this part's blocks.
The fix is outside room-22: the shell has to stop owning the furnishable air, or the lock has to allow it. I did not edit shell.mjs or the build library.
left: REFUSED (21 writes, all of them): the lock is `owned` in build.mjs runParts, and it counts every cell an earlier part wrote, air included. parts/shell.mjs `box()` (line ~26-28) fills x27..68 z43..60 y4..16 with air, and the room box x55..60 z54..60 y11..16 sits inside it. A dump with MCD_PARTS_CELLS puts all 252 cells of the box under 'mansion shell'. Any room part that furnishes these cells gets the same refusal.

Needs an owner decision, not a room-22 edit: (a) shell.mjs leaves room interiors unowned (for example, stops writing air there and lets rooms carve or assume air), or (b) runParts treats earlier air as free for later parts. Option (a) is the one in keeping with 'only add into air'. Until one lands, rooms 1..37 would all refuse the same way.

OFF-PALETTE for room-22 has not been checked by the tool; by reading, its ids (chest, red_carpet, barrel, flower_pot, lantern, red_bed, iron_chain) are all in palette.json. Re-run make.sh after the lock is fixed to confirm.
The part's intent is unchanged and still unbuilt: bed on the west wall, dresser chests on the north wall, red rug, barrel nightstand and side table, hanging lanterns at (57,16,57) and (60,16,54).

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owns the refused cells: I ran a one-off node script on the MCD_PARTS_CELLS dump to count the owners of the 252 cells in the room box.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one ad-hoc script; the refusal line names only the first 8 cells and never the owner
waste.tool: runParts' REFUSED line should name the owning part for each refused cell (for example 'owned by mansion shell') and print a per-part count, so the lock's cause shows up in the same line and no dump is needed.

waste.what: Checking the palette for room-22 by eye, since the palette check is skipped for any write that the lock refuses first.
waste.cost: one read of palette.json and the part; no tool run
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`/`mcd check` pass over the part's own layers() calls, run before the lock, would report off-palette ids and the room box's ownership together, so a refused part still gets its palette report.

companions.task: Fit the bedroom once the shell releases the room's air: the bed on the west wall, the two-chest dresser on the north wall, and the barrel nightstand and side table with their lanterns and flower pot. The joiner would also check the north and east doorway lanes stay clear.
